after_fields.mode_of_action_notes: CURATOR: 1,8-Diazaanthraquinone natural-product antibiotic of the antifolate/thymidylate-synthase-inhibitor diazaquinomycin family from marine-derived Streptomyces sp. F001 and Micromonospora sp. B006 that selectively inhibits Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv growth and replication (MIC = 0.04 ug/mL; Mullowney et al. 2015, DOI:10.1021/acsinfecdis.5b00005, PMID:25893226; Braesel et al. 2018, DOI:10.1021/acs.jnatprod.8b00394, PMID:30110167).

after_molecular_targets.target_label: mycobacterial folate-dependent thymidylate biosynthesis and replication
after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Whole-cell Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv growth-inhibition and drug-resistant panel profiling of diazaquinomycin H (MABA MIC90 = 0.04 ug/mL; LORA MIC90 = 0.07 ug/mL; Mullowney et al. 2015, DOI:10.1021/acsinfecdis.5b00005, PMID:25893226; Braesel et al. 2018, DOI:10.1021/acs.jnatprod.8b00394, PMID:30110167).

evidence.snippet: Mullowney et al. isolated the 1,8-diazaanthraquinone antibiotics diazaquinomycins H and J from Streptomyces sp. F001 and demonstrated potent, selective antitubercular activity against replicating and nonreplicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv (MIC = 0.04 and 0.07 ug/mL) and monoresistant M. tuberculosis strains.
evidence.notes: Mullowney et al. 2015 (ACS Infect Dis 1:168-174; PMID:25893226) isolated diazaquinomycin H and demonstrated nanomolar-to-submicromolar selective growth inhibition of Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv (MABA MIC = 0.04 ug/mL) within the antifolate/thymidylate-synthase-inhibitor diazaquinomycin scaffold class.

Braesel et al. 2018 (J Nat Prod 81:2280-2287; PMID:30110167) identified the daq biosynthetic gene cluster for diazaquinomycins H and J in Micromonospora sp. B006 and confirmed their selective antitubercular activity.

added_history_event.changes: Curated biosynthesis_origin (NATURAL_PRODUCT), mode_of_action (FOLATE_PATHWAY_INHIBITION, MICROBIAL_TARGET), and primary-literature molecular_targets entry for mycobacterial folate-dependent thymidylate biosynthesis and replication (BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS, DOWNSTREAM_AFFECTED_PROCESS) backed by DOI:10.1021/acsinfecdis.5b00005 (PMID:25893226) and DOI:10.1021/acs.jnatprod.8b00394 (PMID:30110167; issue #1307).

after_fields.mode_of_action_notes: CURATOR: 19-Residue cyclic lipodepsipeptide antibiotic of the pore-forming tolaasin/sessilin family from Pseudomonas sp. QS1027 that disrupts Gram-positive bacterial cell-envelope integrity and acts synergistically with co-secreted mupirocin against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Arp et al. 2018, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1721790115, PMID:29592954).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Gram-positive bacterial susceptibility, Bacillus subtilis and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) growth inhibition, and synergistic checkerboard assays of the cyclic lipodepsipeptide jessenipeptin with mupirocin (Arp et al. 2018, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1721790115, PMID:29592954).

evidence.snippet: Arp et al. isolated the 19-amino-acid cyclic lipodepsipeptide jessenipeptin from Pseudomonas sp. QS1027 and demonstrated potent Gram-positive antibacterial activity and synergistic activity with mupirocin against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
evidence.notes: Arp et al. 2018 (Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 115:3758-3763; PMID:29592954) characterized jessenipeptin as an amphiphilic cyclic lipodepsipeptide of the membrane-disrupting tolaasin/sessilin family that targets Gram-positive bacteria including MRSA and synergizes with mupirocin.

added_history_event.changes: Curated biosynthesis_origin (NATURAL_PRODUCT), mode_of_action (MEMBRANE_DISRUPTION, MICROBIAL_TARGET), and primary-literature molecular_targets entry for Gram-positive bacterial cytoplasmic membrane (MEMBRANE, ATTACKED_COMPONENT) backed by DOI:10.1073/pnas.1721790115 (PMID:29592954; issue #1307).

after_fields.mode_of_action_notes: CURATOR: C-nucleoside natural-product antibiotic (oxazinomycin) whose intracellularly phosphorylated 5'-triphosphate metabolite incorporates into nascent RNA in place of UTP and arrests bacterial and eukaryotic DNA-directed RNA polymerase transcription elongation at polythymidine sequences (Prajapati et al. 2019, DOI:10.1093/nar/gkz782, PMID:31535140; Kong et al. 2019, DOI:10.1016/j.isci.2019.11.037, PMID:31816530).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: In vitro transcription elongation and nascent RNA incorporation assays with purified Escherichia coli DNA-directed RNA polymerase and oxazinomycin (minimycin) 5'-triphosphate (Prajapati et al. 2019, DOI:10.1093/nar/gkz782, PMID:31535140; Kong et al. 2019, DOI:10.1016/j.isci.2019.11.037, PMID:31816530).

evidence.snippet: Prajapati et al. demonstrated that the 5'-triphosphate of the C-nucleoside antibiotic oxazinomycin (minimycin) is incorporated into nascent RNA by Escherichia coli RNA polymerase in place of UTP and arrests transcription elongation at polythymidine tracts.
evidence.notes: Prajapati et al. 2019 (Nucleic Acids Res 47:10296-10312; PMID:31535140) established that oxazinomycin (minimycin) 5'-triphosphate serves as a substrate for purified Escherichia coli DNA-directed RNA polymerase and blocks transcription elongation.

Kong et al. 2019 (iScience 22:430-440; PMID:31816530) elucidated the min biosynthetic gene cluster and MinT/MinC self-resistance determinants for minimycin (oxazinomycin) in Streptomyces hygroscopicus.

added_history_event.changes: Curated biosynthesis_origin (NATURAL_PRODUCT), mode_of_action (NUCLEIC_ACID_SYNTHESIS_INHIBITION, HOST_SHARED_TARGET), and primary-literature molecular_targets entry for DNA-directed RNA polymerase complex (GO:0000428, PROTEIN_COMPLEX, DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET) backed by DOI:10.1093/nar/gkz782 (PMID:31535140) and DOI:10.1016/j.isci.2019.11.037 (PMID:31816530; issue #1307).

after_fields.mode_of_action_notes: CURATOR: 16-Membered macrodiolide cation-ionophore antibiotic from Streptomyces alboniger that mediates transmembrane alkali-metal cation transport and disrupts Gram-positive bacterial and mycobacterial cytoplasmic membrane ion gradients (Natsume et al. 1995, DOI:10.7164/antibiotics.48.1159, PMID:7490225; Ren and Wu 2009, DOI:10.1021/ol902290v, PMID:19924823).

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Gram-positive bacterial susceptibility and macrodiolide cation-ionophore membrane-transport structure-activity characterization of pamamycin congeners including pamamycin-621A (Natsume et al. 1995, DOI:10.7164/antibiotics.48.1159, PMID:7490225; Ren and Wu 2009, DOI:10.1021/ol902290v, PMID:19924823).

evidence.snippet: Natsume et al. characterized the structure-activity relationships of pamamycin macrodiolide homologues from Streptomyces alboniger, showing that the dimethylamino-substituted 16-membered macrodiolide ionophore scaffold mediates antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.
evidence.notes: Natsume et al. 1995 (J Antibiot 48:1159-1166; PMID:7490225) established the cation-ionophore and membrane-depolarizing structure-activity relationships of pamamycin macrodiolide antibiotics against Gram-positive bacteria.
Ren and Wu 2009 (Org Lett 11:5638-5641; PMID:19924823) completed the total synthesis and stereochemical verification of the 16-membered macrodiolide antibiotic pamamycin-621A.

after_molecular_targets.experimental_context: Purified bacterial DNA gyrase DNA supercoiling and topoisomerase IV decatenation IC50 inhibition assays and GyrA/ParC QRDR mutant-panel susceptibility profiling of enoxacin alongside comparator fluoroquinolones (Takei et al. 2001, DOI:10.1128/AAC.45.12.3544-3547.2001, PMID:11709337).

evidence.snippet: Takei et al. determined the inhibitory activities (IC50s) of enoxacin and 15 other quinolones against purified bacterial DNA gyrase supercoiling and topoisomerase IV decatenation and correlated enzyme inhibition with MIC shifts across defined GyrA and ParC QRDR mutants.
evidence.notes: Takei et al. 2001 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 45:3544-3547; PMID:11709337) measured direct inhibition of bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV by enoxacin and established target-mutation resistance shifts across GyrA and ParC QRDR variants.
